summary.text: A woman in her 70s had IgG multiple myeloma that initially arose from monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance in 2000. She achieved clinical remission after bortezomib/dexamethasone and lenalidomide/dexamethasone cycles, underwent an autologous bone marrow transplant in December 2020, and remains on daratumumab maintenance after discontinuing pomalidomide because of severe CIPN. Her bilateral lower extremity neuropathy had lasted 6 years with minimal benefit from several prior therapies.

At initial evaluation for Scrambler Therapy she reported neuropathic pain of 5/10 in the right foot and 7/10 in the left foot, walked with a walker because of a slow and unsteady gait, had been largely homebound for years and had significantly impaired activities of daily living such as cooking. Scrambler Therapy was given over a series of sessions, with electrodes placed over the L4, L5, S1 and S2 dermatomes.

Her pain decreased after 3 sessions, and her numbness fell to 2/10 bilaterally by the fifth session, allowing her to resume dancing without a walker, then to 1/10 by session 8 and stayed low in the following weeks. She considers 3–4/10 tolerable, said the outcome exceeded expectations, has become more active in her community and is planning to travel with her daughter.
